description: BPSC TRE Computer Science Model Test Paper 04 containing 150 questions across Language, General Studies, and Computer Science.

questions.questionText: He is _______ European citizen working in New Delhi.
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Although 'European' begins with the vowel letter 'E', its phonetic pronunciation begins with the consonant sound /j/ ('yu'), so the indefinite article 'a' is used.

questions.questionText: The teacher asked the students to look _______ the word in the dictionary.
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb 'look up' means to search for information or a word in a reference book such as a dictionary.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not an astronomical object?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A lighthouse is a terrestrial coastal navigational tower, whereas comets and asteroids are celestial bodies.

questions.questionText: A person who compiles a dictionary is called a:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A lexicographer is a person whose job is writing, compiling, and editing dictionaries.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an antonym of "TRANSPARENT"?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: 'Transparent' means allowing light to pass through clearly, and its direct antonym is 'Opaque'.

questions.questionText: If day before yesterday was Thursday, what day will it be tomorrow?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: If day before yesterday was Thursday, yesterday was Friday, today is Saturday, and tomorrow will be Sunday.

questions.questionText: Which of the following words is correctly spelled?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The correct standard spelling is 'Bureaucracy'.

questions.questionText: Sister of one's husband is called:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A husband's sister (nanad) is designated as sister-in-law.

questions.questionText: 'क्ष, त्र, ज्ञ, श्र' किस श्रेणी के व्यंजन हैं?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: दो व्यंजनों के परस्पर मेल से बनने के कारण क्ष, त्र, ज्ञ और श्र को संयुक्त व्यंजन कहा जाता है।

questions.questionText: 'महोत्सव' शब्द का सही संधि-विच्छेद क्या होगा?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: महा + उत्सव = महोत्सव (आ + उ = ओ), जो गुण स्वर संधि का उदाहरण है।

questions.questionText: 'दशानन' में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: दश हैं आनन जिसके अर्थात् रावण; यहाँ अन्य पद प्रधान होने के कारण बहुव्रीहि समास है।

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द 'आकाश' का पर्यायवाची है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: व्योम, गगन और अंबर तीनों ही आकाश के पर्यायवाची शब्द हैं, अतः 'उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक' सही है।

questions.questionText: 'स्थावर' शब्द का विलोम शब्द क्या है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'स्थावर' (स्थिर रहने वाला) का सटीक विलोम शब्द 'जंगम' (चलने-फिरने वाला) होता है।

questions.questionText: 'जिसकी ग्रीवा (गर्दन) सुंदर हो' वाक्यांश के लिए एक शब्द है:
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: सुंदर ग्रीवा वाले व्यक्ति के लिए प्रयुक्त एक शब्द 'सुग्रीव' (सु + ग्रीवा) होता है।

questions.questionText: 'अंधे की लाठी होना' मुहावरे का सही अर्थ क्या है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'अंधे की लाठी होना' का अर्थ असहाय व्यक्ति का एकमात्र सहारा या अवलंब होना होता है।

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित में से शुद्ध वर्तनी वाला शब्द कौन-सा है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: उद् + ज्वल के योग से बनने वाले शब्द की शुद्ध वर्तनी 'उज्ज्वल' (दोनों 'ज' आधे) है।

questions.questionText: 'वृक्ष पर पक्षी बैठे हैं।' वाक्य में 'वृक्ष पर' में कौन-सा कारक है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: संज्ञा के जिस रूप से क्रिया के आधार (स्थान) का बोध होता है, उसे अधिकरण कारक (चिह्न: में, पर) कहते हैं।

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित में से देशज शब्द कौन-सा है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: लोटा, पगड़ी और खिड़की तीनों ही क्षेत्रीय बोलियों से हिंदी में आए देशज शब्द हैं।

questions.questionText: 'पवन' शब्द का सही संधि-विच्छेद क्या होगा?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: अयादि स्वर संधि के नियमानुसार 'ओ' के बाद भिन्न स्वर आने पर 'अव्' बनता है: पो + अन = पवन।

questions.questionText: "पीपर पात सरिस मन डोला" पंक्ति में कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: यहाँ 'सरिस' वाचक शब्द के माध्यम से मन की तुलना पीपल के पत्ते से की गई है, अतः उपमा अलंकार है।

questions.questionText: 'त्रिफला' शब्द में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'तीन फलों का समाहार'—यहाँ पहला पद संख्यावाचक होने के कारण द्विगु समास है।

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द पुल्लिंग है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: हिंदी व्याकरण में 'दही' को सदैव पुल्लिंग माना जाता है (जैसे- दही खट्टा है)।

questions.questionText: 'अधजल गगरी छलकत जाए' लोकोक्ति का सही अर्थ है:
questions.optionA: अल्प ज्ञान वाला व्यक्ति अधिक दिखावा करता है
questions.optionC: काम न जानना और बहाने बनाना
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: इस लोकोक्ति का भावार्थ है कि कम ज्ञान या सीमित योग्यता वाला व्यक्ति बढ़-चढ़कर अधिक प्रदर्शन करता है।

questions.questionText: 'उत्थान' का विलोम शब्द क्या है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'उत्थान' का विपरीतार्थक शब्द 'पतन' होता है।

questions.questionText: 'आँखें चार होना' मुहावरे का सही अर्थ है:
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'आँखें चार होना' मुहावरे का अर्थ परस्पर आमने-सामने होना या नजरें मिलना होता है।

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द 'कमल' का पर्यायवाची नहीं है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'वारिद' बादल का पर्यायवाची शब्द है, जबकि अरविंद और जलज कमल के पर्यायवाची हैं।

questions.questionText: 'प्रत्युपकार' शब्द में कौन-सा उपसर्ग लगा है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: प्रति + उपकार = प्रत्युपकार (यण् संधि)। इसमें मूल उपसर्ग 'प्रति' है।

questions.questionText: 'जो कानून के विरुद्ध हो' वाक्यांश के लिए एक शब्द है:
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'अवैध' और 'गैरकानूनी' दोनों ही कानून के विरुद्ध आचरण के लिए समानार्थी शब्द हैं, अतः विकल्प (D) सही है।

questions.questionText: 'घोड़ा तेज दौड़ता है।' वाक्य में 'तेज' किस प्रकार का पद है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'तेज' शब्द दौड़ने की रीति या ढंग को स्पष्ट करता है, अतः यह रीतिवाचक क्रियाविशेषण है।

questions.questionText: 'दांतों तले उंगली दबाना' मुहावरे का क्या अर्थ है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'दांतों तले उंगली दबाना' मुहावरा आश्चर्य या विस्मय प्रकट करने के अर्थ में प्रयोग किया जाता है।

questions.questionText: The sum of two numbers is 75 and their difference is 15. The ratio of the two numbers is:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Let numbers be x and y. x + y = 75, x - y = 15. Adding gives 2x = 90 => x = 45, y = 30. Ratio = 45:30 = 3:2.

questions.questionText: A man sells an article for Rs. 1,440 and gains 20%. What was the cost price of the article?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: The diagonal of a square is $10\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$. Its area is:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Side of square = Diagonal / sqrt(2) = 10 cm. Area = side^2 = 10^2 = 100 cm^2.

questions.questionText: The compound interest on Rs. 10,000 for 2 years at 10% per annum compounded annually is:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: A car covers a distance of 180 km in 4 hours. How much distance will it cover in 7 hours at the same speed?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Speed = 180 / 4 = 45 km/h. Distance in 7 hours = 45 * 7 = 315 km.

questions.questionText: If $3^{x+3} = 243$, then the value of $x$ is:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: How many three-digit natural numbers are completely divisible by 7?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Three-digit numbers range from 100 to 999. First is 105 and last is 994. Count = ((994 - 105) / 7) + 1 = 127 + 1 = 128.

questions.questionText: The mean of 10 observations was calculated as 40. It was later found that one observation was misread as 54 instead of 45. The corrected mean is:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Initial sum = 40 * 10 = 400. Correct sum = 400 - 54 + 45 = 391. Correct mean = 391 / 10 = 39.1.

questions.questionText: Which gas is filled in electric light bulbs to prevent the tungsten filament from oxidizing?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Inert gases like Argon as well as Nitrogen are filled in incandescent bulbs to retard filament evaporation and prevent oxidation.

questions.questionText: A pencil dipped partially in water appears bent at the interface. This phenomenon is caused by:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Light rays bending when transitioning across the boundary between water and air is due to refraction.

questions.questionText: Which instrument is used to measure atmospheric pressure?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A barometer is used to measure atmospheric pressure.

questions.questionText: Which human blood group is known as the "Universal Recipient"?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Individuals with AB positive blood have A, B, and Rh antigens and no plasma antibodies, allowing them to receive red blood cells from any blood type.

questions.questionText: Bleaching powder is chemically known as:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Bleaching powder (CaOCl2) is known chemically as calcium hypochlorite as well as calcium oxychloride.

questions.questionText: Which hormone controls the level of glucose in human blood?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Insulin, secreted by beta cells of the pancreatic islets, facilitates glucose absorption and lowers blood sugar levels.

questions.questionText: What is the value of acceleration due to gravity ($g$) at the centre of the Earth?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: At the exact centre of the Earth, gravitational attraction from surrounding mass cancels out symmetrically, resulting in g = 0 m/s^2.

questions.questionText: Which metal is the most ductile and malleable of all elements?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Gold (Au) possesses the highest malleability and ductility among all known metals.

questions.questionText: On which date is 'National Science Day' celebrated every year in India?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: National Science Day is celebrated on 28 February to commemorate Sir C. V. Raman's discovery of the Raman Effect in 1928.

questions.questionText: Who is the current Chief Election Commissioner of India?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Rajiv Kumar served as the 25th Chief Election Commissioner of India.

questions.questionText: Which country will host the 2026 FIFA Football World Cup jointly?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The 2026 FIFA World Cup will be jointly hosted by sixteen cities across the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

questions.questionText: India's first indigenously developed payment app BHIM is based on:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: BHIM (Bharat Interface for Money) was developed by NPCI based on the Unified Payments Interface (UPI).

questions.questionText: Which city in India has been recognized as the cleanest city for the 7th consecutive year in Swachh Survekshan?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Indore secured the cleanest city title for the 7th time in Swachh Survekshan 2023, sharing the top rank jointly with Surat.

questions.questionText: What is the chemical name of "Baking Soda"?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Baking soda is chemically sodium hydrogen carbonate or sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3).

questions.questionText: Which state in India is known as the "Spice Garden of India"?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Kerala is traditionally called the 'Spice Garden of India' due to its extensive cultivation of pepper, cardamom, and cinnamon.

questions.questionText: Which river originates from the Amarkantak plateau in Madhya Pradesh?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Both the westward-flowing Narmada and the northward-flowing Son rivers originate from the Amarkantak hills.

questions.questionText: Which strait separates India from Sri Lanka?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait and Gulf of Mannar lie between the southeastern coast of Tamil Nadu and northern Sri Lanka.

questions.questionText: In Bihar, the thermal power plant at Kahalgaon is situated in which district?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Kahalgaon Super Thermal Power Station, operated by NTPC, is located in the Bhagalpur district of Bihar.

questions.questionText: What is the sex ratio of Bihar according to the Census 2011?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: As per Census 2011, the sex ratio of Bihar is 918 females per 1,000 males.

questions.questionText: Which district of Bihar has the highest population density as per Census 2011?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Sheohar has the highest population density among all districts in Bihar at 1,880 persons per sq km.

questions.questionText: Rajgir, the ancient capital of Magadha, is surrounded by how many hills?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The ancient valley city of Rajgir (Girivraja) is surrounded by five hills: Ratnagiri, Vipulagiri, Vaibhargiri, Sonagiri, and Udaygiri.

questions.questionText: The Bhimbandh Wildlife Sanctuary is located in which district of Bihar?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Bhimbandh Wildlife Sanctuary is situated in the Kharagpur hills region of Munger district.

questions.questionText: Who was the founder of the 'Brahmo Samaj' in 1828?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha (later Brahmo Samaj) in Calcutta in August 1828.

questions.questionText: Who coined the popular slogan "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak proclaimed this historic slogan during the Home Rule movement.

questions.questionText: The historic Lucknow Pact of 1916 was signed between:
questions.optionA: Indian National Congress and the Muslim League
questions.optionB: British Government and Indian National Congress
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The 1916 Lucknow session reunited Moderates and Extremists inside the Congress and achieved a political pact with the All-India Muslim League.

questions.questionText: Who was the Governor-General of India when the Revolt of 1857 broke out?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Lord Canning was the Governor-General of India during 1857 and later became India's first Viceroy under the Government of India Act 1858.

questions.questionText: Who founded the 'Ghadar Party' in San Francisco (USA) in 1913?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Lala Har Dayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna, and other expatriates founded the Pacific Coast Hindustan Association (Ghadar Party) in 1913.

questions.questionText: Who presided over the historic Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress in 1929 where 'Poorna Swaraj' was declared?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the December 1929 Lahore session where the Poorna Swaraj resolution was passed.

questions.questionText: In Bihar, who was elected as the leader of the First Congress Ministry formed in 1937?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Dr. Sri Krishna Sinha became the Premier (Chief Minister) leading the first Congress ministry in Bihar in July 1937.

questions.questionText: Who was the editor of the nationalist bi-weekly journal 'Biharee' launched in 1906?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Babu Mahesh Narayan served as the founding editor of 'The Biharee', advocating statehood for Bihar.

questions.questionText: The Chuar Rebellion (1766–1816) predominantly affected which parts of ancient Bihar and Bengal?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Chuar (Bhumij) rebellion took place in the Jungle Mahals region spanning Midnapore, Bankura, and Manbhum.

questions.questionText: Who was the first interim President of the Constituent Assembly of India in December 1946?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was elected as the temporary interim Chairman of the Constituent Assembly on 9 December 1946 based on French convention.

questions.questionText: What is the minimum number of 2-to-1 multiplexers required to implement a 4-to-1 multiplexer?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Two 2-to-1 MUXes are needed in the first stage, followed by one 2-to-1 MUX in the second stage, totaling 3.

questions.questionText: What is the simplified expression for $F = A'B + AB + AB'$ using Boolean laws?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: In digital circuits, Gray code is predominantly categorized as a:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Gray code is an unweighted unit-distance code where two successive values differ by exactly one binary bit.

questions.questionText: The decimal value of the Excess-3 code 1001 is:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: 1001 in binary is 9. To obtain the decimal value from Excess-3, subtract 3: 9 - 3 = 6.

questions.questionText: What type of flip-flop is constructed by tying the $J$ and $K$ inputs of a JK flip-flop together?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Connecting J and K together forms a T flip-flop, toggling state when T=1 and holding state when T=0.

questions.questionText: How many state transitions are possible in a 3-bit Johnson (twisted ring) counter?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: An n-stage Johnson counter produces 2n states. For n = 3, it cycles through 2 * 3 = 6 states.

questions.questionText: An instruction cycle primarily consists of which sub-cycles in sequence?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The core basic instruction execution sequence alternates between Fetch and Execute phases.

questions.questionText: Which of the following registers keeps track of processor status and conditional flags (Carry, Zero, Sign, Overflow)?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Program Status Word (PSW) or Flag Register records the condition flags resulting from arithmetic and logic operations.

questions.questionText: In an instruction format of a 16-bit processor, if 4 bits are allocated for Opcode, how many distinct instructions can be supported?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: With 4 bits in the opcode field, 2^4 = 16 distinct operational instructions can be represented.

questions.questionText: What is a "vector interrupt"?
questions.optionA: An interrupt where the interrupting device supplies its own interrupt service routine (ISR) address directly to the CPU
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In vectored interrupts, the peripheral device provides a vector address pointing to its specific interrupt service routine.

questions.questionText: Which memory cache mapping technique allows a block of main memory to be loaded into any one of a restricted set of $k$ lines in cache?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In k-way set associative mapping, the cache is partitioned into sets, each containing k lines, allowing placement anywhere within a mapped set.

questions.questionText: In pipelined processors, what technique is used to resolve data hazards caused by Read-After-Write (RAW) dependencies without stalling?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Operand forwarding (data bypassing) routes results directly from ALU/memory pipeline registers to earlier stages to avoid stall cycles.

questions.questionText: In the 8085 microprocessor, which pin is used to demultiplex the lower-order address/data bus ($AD_0 - AD_7$)?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Address Latch Enable (ALE) signal goes high during the T1 cycle to latch the lower 8-bit memory address into an external 74LS373 latch.

questions.questionText: Which optical storage disc utilizes a blue-violet laser with a wavelength of 405 nm?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Blu-ray discs use a 405 nm blue-violet laser, allowing narrower tracks and higher data density than red-laser DVDs.

questions.questionText: What does the term "Spatial Locality" imply in cache memory design?
questions.optionA: If a memory location is referenced, nearby memory locations are likely to be referenced in the near future
questions.optionB: A referenced memory location is likely to be referenced repeatedly in a loop
questions.optionC: Memory addresses are distributed uniformly across DRAM
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Spatial locality states that accessing a memory word implies high probability of accessing adjacent words shortly.

questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Modifying variable 'a' more than once between sequence points results in undefined behavior per ISO C specifications.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about a C union?
questions.optionA: All members share the same memory location
questions.optionB: Total memory size equals the size of its largest member
questions.optionC: Only one member can contain a valid value at any given time
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: All members of a union share memory, its total size matches its largest field, and only one member is stored at once.

questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: s[0]='B', s[1]='P', s[2]='S', s[3]='C', s[4]='2'. Dereferencing *(p + 4) outputs '2'.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of the volatile qualifier in C/C++?
questions.optionA: To prevent compiler optimization on variables that may be changed by hardware or concurrent threads
questions.optionB: To make variables constant throughout execution
questions.optionC: To allocate variables directly into L1 cache
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The 'volatile' keyword instructs the compiler to avoid caching or optimizing access to variables modified by external hardware or ISRs.

questions.questionText: In C++, which casting operator is safest for performing downcasting of polymorphic base class pointers to derived class pointers?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: dynamic_cast uses RTTI to safely verify downcasts at runtime, returning nullptr if the object is not of the target derived type.

questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Calling fun(5) passes x=5 while y uses its default parameter value 20, resulting in 5 + 20 = 25.

questions.questionText: In C++, which operator is used for dynamic memory deallocation of arrays?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Arrays allocated dynamically using 'new[]' must be released using 'delete[]' to invoke element destructors.

questions.questionText: What is an inline function in C++?
questions.optionA: A function that cannot return any value
questions.optionB: A function whose code is expanded in-line at each point of call by compiler suggestion
questions.optionC: A function defined inside a macro only
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: An inline function suggests to the compiler to substitute the function body at the point of each call to reduce call overhead.

questions.questionText: Which of the following members of a base class are NEVER inherited by a derived class in C++?
questions.optionC: Friend functions of the base class
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Constructors, destructors, overloaded assignment operators, and friend functions are not inherited by derived classes in C++.

questions.questionText: A class template in C++ enables which programming paradigm?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Class and function templates provide generic programming by parameterizing classes over types.

questions.questionText: What is the role of the explicit keyword when applied to a single-parameter constructor in C++?
questions.optionA: It forces the constructor to be declared virtual
questions.optionB: It prevents implicit conversions and copy-initialization
questions.optionC: It allows the constructor to be called without arguments
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Marking a constructor as 'explicit' stops the compiler from applying implicit conversions during assignments.

questions.questionText: In C++, what mechanism does the compiler use at runtime to resolve virtual function calls?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Polymorphic classes maintain a virtual method table (vtable) and each object carries an internal vptr pointer.

questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Since x=10 > 5, 'throw x' is triggered and intercepted by catch(int e), printing 'Caught: 10'.

questions.questionText: Which of the following operators cannot be overloaded as a non-member (friend) function in C++?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In C++, operator=, operator(), operator[], and operator-> must be non-static member functions and cannot be friend functions.

questions.questionText: What is the fundamental purpose of namespaces in C++?
questions.optionA: To prevent identifier naming collisions in large software projects
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Namespaces organize code into logical scopes to prevent naming conflicts between libraries and modules.

questions.questionText: What does the sizeof operator evaluate in C/C++?
questions.optionA: The number of bits in a data type at runtime
questions.optionB: The memory size in bytes allocated for an expression or type at compile time
questions.optionC: The length of a null-terminated string
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: sizeof is a compile-time operator that returns the total storage size in bytes of a data type or expression.

questions.questionText: In C++, when a base class pointer points to a derived class object, calling a non-virtual function results in:
questions.optionA: Base class version being executed (Early/Static binding)
questions.optionB: Derived class version being executed (Late binding)
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Non-virtual calls are bound statically based on the pointer's declared type, invoking the base class implementation.

questions.questionText: Which standard stream object in C++ is unbuffered and used for error reporting?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: std::cerr writes unbuffered error output directly to standard error, ensuring messages display immediately.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about copy constructors in C++?
questions.optionA: It must take its parameter as a reference (usually const ClassName&)
questions.optionB: If not provided, a default member-wise shallow copy constructor is synthesized
questions.optionC: It is invoked when an object is passed by value to a function
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: All three statements correctly characterize copy constructor definition, synthesis, and pass-by-value invocation.

questions.questionText: In standard C++, which file mode opens an existing file and positions the file pointer at the end of the file?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: ios::ate (at end) opens a stream and immediately positions the read/write pointer at the end of the file.

questions.questionText: What is the time complexity of building a Binary Heap of $N$ elements from an arbitrary unsorted array using the bottom-up heapify procedure?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Building a heap bottom-up with Floyd's build-heap algorithm sums the heights of nodes, bounding overall time to O(N).

questions.questionText: Which of the following algorithms is an example of an In-place, Stable sorting algorithm?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Insertion Sort sorts in place with O(1) auxiliary space and preserves the relative order of equal keys (stable).

questions.questionText: What is the auxiliary space complexity of standard Depth First Search (DFS) on a graph using recursion?
questions.optionA: $O(V)$ due to call stack and visited array
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Recursive DFS requires O(V) auxiliary space to track visited vertices and maintain recursive stack depth.

questions.questionText: In a Red-Black Tree, what is the maximum possible height of a tree containing $N$ internal nodes?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Due to balancing properties (no two red nodes adjacent), a red-black tree with N internal nodes has a maximum height of 2 * log2(N + 1).

questions.questionText: Which data structure is used internally by the Disjoint Set Union (DSU) data structure to achieve nearly $O(1)$ amortized find and union operations?
questions.optionB: Forest of Trees with Union by Rank and Path Compression
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: DSU represents disjoint sets as a forest of trees using path compression and union by rank to achieve inverse Ackermann amortized time.

questions.questionText: What is the recurrence relation for the standard Merge Sort algorithm?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Merge sort divides the problem into two subproblems of size N/2 and merges them in linear time: T(N) = 2T(N/2) + Θ(N).

questions.questionText: The number of leaf nodes in a strictly (full) binary tree with $L$ internal nodes is:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In any strictly binary tree where every internal node has exactly 2 children, the number of leaf nodes equals internal nodes + 1 (L + 1).

questions.questionText: What is the primary difference between a B-Tree and a B+ Tree?
questions.optionA: In a B+ Tree, data records/pointers are stored only at the leaf nodes, which are linked sequentially
questions.optionB: In a B-Tree, keys can only be strings
questions.optionC: B+ Trees do not permit duplicate values
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In a B+ tree, internal nodes store only indexing keys, and all data pointers reside in leaf nodes connected by a linked list.

questions.questionText: What data structure is utilized in Kahn's algorithm for Topological Sorting of a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)?
questions.optionA: Stack or Queue storing nodes with in-degree zero
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Kahn's algorithm initializes a queue/stack containing all vertices with in-degree 0 and iteratively decrements neighbor in-degrees.

questions.questionText: What is the worst-case time complexity of searching an element in a Skip List with $N$ elements?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: While average search in a skip list is O(log N), poor randomized coin flips can degenerate the levels to a linear list of O(N).

questions.questionText: In Huffman Coding, what type of tree is constructed to generate prefix-free variable-length codes?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A Huffman tree is a full binary tree where every non-leaf node has exactly two children.

questions.questionText: An algorithm whose running time is governed by the recurrence $T(N) = 4T(N/2) + O(N)$ has a time complexity of:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: By Master Theorem, a=4, b=2, c=1. log_b(a) = log_2(4) = 2 > c. Case 1 applies, yielding Θ(N^2).

questions.questionText: What is the minimum number of comparisons needed to find the maximum and minimum elements simultaneously in an array of $N$ numbers?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: By processing elements in pairs and comparing against current min and max, the total comparisons are bounded by ceil(3N/2) - 2.

questions.questionText: Which string-matching algorithm preprocesses the pattern to construct a "prefix function" ($\pi$ table) to achieve $O(N + M)$ time?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The KMP algorithm constructs a longest prefix-suffix (LPS) array to avoid redundant character re-comparisons.

questions.questionText: In hashing, what happens when two different keys hash to the same table index?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: When a hash function maps two distinct keys to the same index, a hash collision occurs.

questions.questionText: What is the degree of a database relation?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The degree of a relation is the total number of attributes (columns); the cardinality is the total number of tuples (rows).

questions.questionText: Which SQL constraint ensures that all values in a column are distinct and not null?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A PRIMARY KEY constraint enforces both uniqueness and NOT NULL on the constrained column(s).

questions.questionText: In relational algebra, which operator is mathematically non-commutative?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Set difference is non-commutative: R - S is generally not equal to S - R.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about correlated subqueries in SQL?
questions.optionA: The inner query executes independently only once
questions.optionB: The inner query references a column from the outer query and executes once for each row evaluated by the outer query
questions.optionC: Correlated subqueries can never be written using joins
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A correlated subquery references values from the enclosing query, requiring re-evaluation for every outer table row.

questions.questionText: Fourth Normal Form (4NF) is designed to handle which type of dependency?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A relation is in 4NF if it is in BCNF and contains no non-trivial multivalued dependencies (MVD).

questions.questionText: What does the "Write-Ahead Logging" (WAL) protocol mandate in database crash recovery?
questions.optionA: Data blocks must be written to disk before log records
questions.optionB: Log records describing changes must be flushed to non-volatile storage before corresponding database disk pages are written
questions.optionC: Logs are written only after transaction commit is confirmed
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: WAL requires that log updates be flushed to non-volatile disk before the modified dirty data pages are written to disk.

questions.questionText: Which isolation level in SQL prevents Dirty Reads, Non-repeatable Reads, and Phantom Reads completely?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Serializable isolation is the highest level, preventing dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, and phantom read anomalies.

questions.questionText: What is a "phantom read" anomaly in database transactions?
questions.optionA: A transaction reads data that has been modified but uncommitted by another transaction
questions.optionB: A transaction re-executes a query reading a set of rows and finds that new matching rows have been inserted by another committed transaction
questions.optionC: A transaction reads different values of the same row on consecutive reads
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A phantom read occurs when a transaction queries a range of rows twice and sees new matching records committed by another transaction in between.

questions.questionText: What is the SQL statement used to remove an entire table's schema, constraints, and data permanently from the database?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: DROP TABLE removes the entire table definition along with its data, indexes, and triggers from the database catalog.

questions.questionText: What type of lock allows multiple transactions to read a data item concurrently, but prevents any transaction from writing to it?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A Shared Lock (S-lock) permits concurrent read operations across multiple transactions while preventing exclusive write locks.

questions.questionText: A B+ tree index is widely preferred over a hash index in relational DBMS primarily because:
questions.optionA: It supports efficient range queries ($<, \le, >, \ge$) as well as point lookups
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: B+ tree leaves form an ordered linked list, making range scans and inequality comparisons efficient compared to hash indexes.

questions.questionText: In an ER diagram, a Weak Entity Set is depicted by:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In Peter Chen's ER notation, weak entity sets are represented using a double-bordered rectangle.

questions.questionText: What is the main cause of "Internal Fragmentation" in memory management?
questions.optionB: Fixed-size partition allocation or paging where a process requests less memory than the allocated block size
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Internal fragmentation arises when fixed memory blocks allocated to a process exceed the requested payload, leaving wasted space inside.

questions.questionText: In Linux operating systems, what is the process with Process ID (PID) 1?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The init system (or systemd in modern Linux distributions) is the first user-space process spawned with PID 1.

questions.questionText: What is the condition known as "Convoy Effect" in CPU scheduling?
questions.optionA: Small processes wait for a long time behind a large CPU-bound process in FCFS scheduling
questions.optionC: CPU switches contexts too frequently in Round Robin
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The convoy effect occurs in FCFS when multiple I/O-bound short tasks wait idly behind a single heavy CPU-bound process.

questions.questionText: Which classical synchronization problem models resource sharing among multiple processes competing for a limited set of identical resources?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Dining Philosophers, Readers-Writers, and Producer-Consumer all model concurrent synchronization and shared resource access.

questions.questionText: What is an "Orphan Process" in Unix?
questions.optionA: A process whose parent process has terminated before the child process
questions.optionB: A process that has no execution code
questions.optionC: A process suspended by the kernel
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: An orphan process is a running child process whose parent has exited; it is reparented to init (PID 1).

questions.questionText: In virtual memory management, the "Dirty Bit" (Modified Bit) in a page table entry indicates:
questions.optionA: The page has experienced an error
questions.optionB: The page has been modified since it was loaded into RAM and must be written back to disk before replacement
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The dirty bit tracks if a page in physical memory has been written to, signaling that disk write-back is required during replacement.

questions.questionText: Which page replacement algorithm achieves the theoretical minimum number of page faults for a given memory access string?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Belady's Optimal Page Replacement replaces the page that will not be used for the longest future duration, minimizing page faults.

questions.questionText: What is a "race condition" in concurrent programming?
questions.optionA: A condition where multiple threads or processes access and manipulate shared data concurrently and the final result depends on the order of execution
questions.optionB: High CPU clock speed causing hardware damage
questions.optionC: Memory running out of heap space
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A race condition occurs when concurrent threads alter shared state without synchronization and the outcome depends on execution timing.

questions.questionText: The disk scheduling algorithm that services all requests in one direction and then immediately returns to the beginning without servicing requests on the return trip is:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: C-SCAN moves the disk arm across to one end servicing requests, then immediately returns to the start without servicing requests on return.

questions.questionText: What is the fundamental role of a device driver in an operating system?
questions.optionA: Providing a standardized software interface between the operating system kernel and specific hardware peripherals
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Device drivers abstract hardware variations, providing standardized system-call interfaces to the operating system kernel.

questions.questionText: Which protocol in the TCP/IP suite is responsible for reporting error conditions and diagnostic queries (e.g., Destination Unreachable, Time Exceeded)?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) communicates network diagnostics and error condition messages.

questions.questionText: What is the size of a MAC (Media Access Control) hardware address?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Standard Ethernet MAC addresses are 48 bits (6 octets) in length, formatted as 12 hexadecimal digits.

questions.questionText: What is the default port number used by HTTPS (Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure)?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Standard plain HTTP uses port 80, whereas encrypted HTTPS uses port 443.

questions.questionText: Which symmetric encryption algorithm is currently recognized as the global standard by NIST?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: NIST adopted the Rijndael block cipher as the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) in 2001.

questions.questionText: In the context of Chomsky's hierarchy of formal languages, which automaton recognizes Context-Free Languages (CFL)?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Pushdown Automata (PDA) are computationally equivalent to Context-Free Grammars and recognize Context-Free Languages.

questions.questionText: What is the Cyclomatic Complexity $V(G)$ of a program control flow graph with $E$ edges, $N$ nodes, and $P$ connected components?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: McCabe's Cyclomatic Complexity formula is V(G) = E - N + 2P.

questions.questionText: In web development, which HTTP request method is designed to be idempotent according to RFC specifications?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: GET, PUT, and DELETE are all idempotent HTTP methods because repeated identical requests produce the same intended server outcome.

questions.questionText: Which metric is most commonly evaluated as an activation function in Deep Neural Networks to alleviate the vanishing gradient problem?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: ReLU maintains a constant derivative of 1 for positive inputs, preventing vanishing gradients in deep backpropagation.
